exposure: Obstetrician demographics (gender, marital status, number of children, birth order)
Opinions on factors contributing to high CS rate (medico-legal conditions, advanced maternal age/IVF, lack of training in instrumental deliveries, maternal request)
outcome: Obstetrician's actual delivery mode for their own children (vaginal vs. CS)
Obstetrician's preferred delivery mode for their own children
Willingness to opt for vaginal birth after cesarean section (VBAC)
Perceived reasons for high CS rates in Greece
cohort: The study included 337 Greek obstetricians who responded to an emailed questionnaire regarding their preferences and choices for the delivery mode of their own children.
finding: Despite a strong preference for normal labor (78.8%) for their own children, the actual cesarean section rate among Greek obstetricians for their first child (44.2%) was found to mirror that of the general population.
mod_finding: Although 78.8% of Greek obstetricians preferred normal labor for their own children, only 55.8% reported a vaginal delivery for their first child, with male and married obstetricians being more likely to prefer vaginal birth, and partner preference influencing both choice and actual delivery mode.
